key_insight: Zero-shot compositional action recognition models often fail not because they can't learn verbs or objects separately, but because they latch onto object-driven 'verb shortcuts' — a bias caused by sparse, skewed compositional supervision and asymmetric learning difficulty between verbs and objects. Targeted diagnostics and training interventions that reduce this shortcutting substantially improve generalization to unseen verb-object combinations.
problem_solved: Addresses the failure of ZS-CAR models to generalize to unseen verb-object compositions by identifying and mitigating object-driven shortcut learning arising from sparsity and asymmetry in compositional supervision.
method: Systematic diagnostic analysis that quantifies object influence on verb predictions and attributes failures to compositional supervision sparsity and asymmetric verb/object learning difficulty.

Design of mitigation interventions (e.g., rebalancing supervision, compositional regularizers, and representation disentangling or object-agnostic training signals) to discourage object-driven shortcut learning.
Empirical evaluation showing that these targeted changes improve zero-shot compositional accuracy and robustness across benchmarks.
impact: Helps researchers and practitioners build video-action models that truly compose verbs and objects instead of exploiting dataset shortcuts, improving robustness and reliability for downstream tasks like robotics, surveillance, and human-computer interaction.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing accuracy on seen vs. unseen verb-object pairs before and after mitigation (shows reduction in performance gap).
Heatmap or Sankey diagram showing object→verb influence strengths to visualize object-driven shortcutting.
Histogram of compositional supervision sparsity/skewness across dataset classes to illustrate the root cause.
Model schematic illustrating disentangled verb/object pathways and the proposed regularizer or object-agnostic training intervention.
paper_title: Why Can't I Open My Drawer? Mitigating Object-Driven Shortcuts in Zero-Shot Compositional Action Recognition
paper_authors: Geo Ahn, Inwoong Lee, Taeoh Kim, Minho Shim, Dongyoon Wee
